# Use a standard Ubuntu 22.04 base image
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, git, OpenMPI, required libraries, and certificates
# libgomp1 is required for OpenMP support at runtime
# ca-certificates are necessary for secure connections (e.g., git clone)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 \
    ca-certificates && \
    # Clean up the apt cache to reduce image size
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for container environments
# Allow running MPI applications as the root user inside the container
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Prevent OpenMPI from using shared memory mechanisms that can cause issues in some container runtimes
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
# Disable help message aggregation which can be problematic in some environments
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
# Use async modex for better scalability in some network environments
ENV OMPI_MCA_pmix_base_async_modex=1

# Create a temporary directory for building the application
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the AMG repository, build the libraries from the top level,
# then build the test executable, copy it to a location on the system PATH,
# and clean up the build directory.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git && \
    # FIX: Build from the top-level AMG directory first to compile required libraries.
    cd AMG && \
    make && \
    # Now, build the test executable which links against the libraries.
    make -C test && \
    cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set a default entrypoint or command to facilitate running the container
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# MiniCluster manifest for running an AMG experiment on AWS CPU instances.
# This configuration runs the specified container and command on a single node.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg-problem2-test
  # The MiniCluster will be created in the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, corresponding to a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the MiniCluster.
  # With size: 1, all 4 tasks will run within the single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Keep pods and logs after the job finishes for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  
  # Enforce strict schema validation for the manifest.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container that will run the HPC job.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute for the experiment.
      # Runs AMG with problem type 2 and a small problem size (4x4x4 grid).
      command: "amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4"
      
      # This container is a worker, not a standalone job launcher.
      # The Flux Operator will wrap the command to run under `flux`.
      launcher: false

manager.name: Build and Deploy AMG2023
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.details:
Clone the latest branch of amg2023. You MUST put amg on the PATH.
You MUST install libgomp1 for libgomp1.so and you MUST NOT run apt-get purge

context.optimize:
Maximize the amg2023 figure of merit. You MUST maximize memory per CPU core. More cores are better.
The trick to optimizing this is THREADING. You MUST force OpenMP and any math libraries to use only one thread per MPI rank. On example is setting OMP_NUM_THREADS to "1". You might also consider setting OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism to "cma" as a conservative builder will set to none.
You MUST choose initial parameters and use the provided function for guidance about what to change. 
The size of the MiniCluster MUST be 1. Tasks MUST be at least 4.
To reduce noise in logging, you can set logging.quiet to true.
If there is a build issue, you can use containers[0].commands.pre to do installation or additional setup
context.resources:
The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. For your optimization you can choose from the following instance types, and you will need to add the correct nodeSelector with the node.kubernetes.io/instance-type label indicating your choice. You are still limited to one node.      
  c7a.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, AMD
  hpc7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  c6in.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
  r7iz.8xlarge, 16 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6g.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton2)
  t3a.2xlarge, 4 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, AMD
  t3.2xlarge, 4 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6id.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, Intel
  c6id.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
  t4g.2xlarge, 8 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton2)

import math
from typing import Dict, Any, Literal
import json

def evaluate_amg_run(
    # Problem size
    problem_size: Any,
    total_ranks: int,
    nodes_used: int,
    # Hardware constraints
    cores_per_node: int,
    memory_gb_per_node: int,
    threading_hint: int,
    current_fom: float,
    threshold: float = 0.90,
    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 4.5e8,
    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 1.0e6,
    dofs_per_gb: float = 1.2e7,
    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.95
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Args:
        problem_size (tuple): The 3D problem grid dimensions (e.g., Px, Py, Pz).
        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.
        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.
        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.
        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.
        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).
        current_fom (float): The measured Figure of Merit (FOM) from the completed run.
        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum FOM (default 0.90).
        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 4.5e8).
        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant modeling communication overhead (default 1.0e6).
        dofs_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (DOFs per GB of RAM, default 1.2e7).
        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.95).

    Returns:
        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.
    """   
    total_dofs = problem_size[0] * problem_size[1] * problem_size[2]
    if total_ranks == 0:
        return {"decision": "RETRY", "reason": "The number of tasks cannot be zero. Suggest using at least one task."}

    # --- 2. Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---
    dofs_per_rank = total_dofs / total_ranks
    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint
    cpu_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node

    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(dofs_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)
    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency
    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_ranks * cpu_per_rank

    performance_ratio = 0.0
    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:
        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom

    estimated_memory_gb = total_dofs / dofs_per_gb
    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used)

    metrics = {
        "performance_ratio": round(performance_ratio, 3),
        "scaling_efficiency": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),
        "memory_utilization": round(memory_utilization, 3),
        "dofs_per_rank": int(dofs_per_rank),
        "theoretical_max_fom": f"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}"
    }
    # --- 3. Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---        
    # Primary STOP condition: Performance is good enough.
    if performance_ratio >= threshold:
        return {
            "decision": "STOP",
            "reason": f"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Primary RETRY condition: Memory is the bottleneck.
    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The problem size is too large for the allocated memory. Suggest significantly reducing the problem size.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Secondary RETRY condition: Scaling is the bottleneck.
    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for "low" efficiency
         return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the problem size per rank is too small. Suggest significantly increasing the problem size to provide more work per rank.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Tertiary RETRY condition: Cores are underutilized on a single node.
    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Suggest increasing the number of tasks to better utilize the hardware.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    # Default RETRY condition: Performance is simply not good enough yet.
    return {
        "decision": "RETRY",
        "reason": f"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Suggest moderately increasing the problem size to improve the work-per-rank and move closer to the optimal FOM.",
        "metrics": metrics
    }
